statement.document_title: Breaking news, and how the end might begin

from_speaker: no longer want to offer all-you-can-eat
customers no longer want to pay for a la carte
our_interpretation: The plain reading is a broad commercial mismatch: major providers were retreating from flat-fee access that accommodates very heavy use, while customers resisted paying separately for that usage.

All-you-can-eat is a metaphor for generous bundled access, not necessarily a contractual promise of literally unlimited computing. Ordinary capped subscriptions neither automatically support nor refute the claim.

Customer resistance can appear in complaints, cancellations, budget restrictions, negotiations or substitution. Falling aggregate spending is not required, and continuing purchases do not alone disprove resistance.
The generalization concerns a broad pattern, not every provider and every customer.

For the ongoing state, use June 1–10, the latest observable calendar month to date. Earlier policies are context unless their operation in this window is established. Later changes cannot establish the June 10 state.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes both a broad retreat by major LLM service providers from generous flat-fee heavy usage and substantial customer resistance to the resulting metered charges by June 10.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that major providers broadly continued to favor generous flat-fee heavy usage, or that customer acceptance of metered charges was broad enough to contradict the asserted resistance. An isolated plan or willing customer is insufficient.
